definition: The Portable Format for Analytics (PFA) is a JSON-based predictive model interchange format conceived and developed by Jim Pivarski.
details: PFA provides a way for analytic applications to describe and exchange predictive models produced by analytics and machine learning algorithms. It supports common models such as logistic regression and decision trees. Version 0.8 was published in 2015. Subsequent versions have been developed by the Data Mining Group. As a predictive model interchange format developed by the Data Mining Group, PFA is complementary to the DMG's XML-based standard called the Predictive Model Markup Language or PMML.

explainer.lead: PFA is a JSON-based interchange format that lets analytics applications describe and exchange predictive models produced by analytics and machine learning algorithms.

tiers.eli5: It is a shared file format that lets one program hand its prediction recipe to another program without either needing to know the other's internals.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers export models such as logistic regression and decision trees into PFA so different tools can execute them; it is complementary to the XML-based PMML rather than a replacement.
tiers.paperLevel: A JSON-based predictive model interchange format conceived by Jim Pivarski and developed by the Data Mining Group (version 0.8 published in 2015), supporting common models such as logistic regression and decision trees.

explainer.example: A decision tree trained in one analytics tool is written as PFA JSON and executed by another application.
